newsitem.title: UK: Fast-food groups face tough Italian market - study.
newsitem.headline: Fast-food groups face tough Italian market - study.

text.p: Fast-food companies trying to establish and expand market share in Italy face tough cultural obstacles, according to a report issued on Thursday by Euromonitor, the market research company.
Anthony Irwin, Euromonitor's reports manager, said it was difficult to penetrate the Italian market, since hamburgers and other fast food had no place in the average Italian's diet.
"Foreign companies wishing to tap into the Italian market have to face both cultural and operational barriers," Irwin told an International Fast Food Symposium in Madrid.

"The cultural factor seems to be precisely why fast food has not taken off in Italy: consumers place the emphasis on the quality and freshness of the food and accord great importance to the meal occasion," Irwin said, in a speech text received in London.
Irwin said the Italian fast-food market registered strong growth in the five years to 1996, with the volume and value of sales both increasing by 100 per cent.
But he said that was from a very low base.
"Placed in context the market has been rather weak," he said.
McDonald's Corp opened only 39 outlets in Italy between 1985 and 1995 and it had had to adapt to local tastes by offering espresso and cappuccino coffee and salad bars to its customers.
Irwin said that there were only two main players in the Italian market: McDonald's and Spizzico, owned by the Autogrill group.
The fast-food market in Italy contrasts sharply with that in the United States, which Irwin believes is reaching saturation point.

"With unit growth of just 2.5 per cent in 1996, there is no doubt that the U.S. fast-food market will become increasingly competitive and develop at a faster pace to the year 2000 as gains in market share or growth become harder to find," he said.
